nodes.label: Poor vision may make traffic harder to recognize, hazards harder to notice and responses slower; the handbook recommends regular eye examinations.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A driver who needs corrective lenses must use them behind the wheel and should avoid dark or tinted corrective lenses at night.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Fatigue means extreme tiredness associated with causes such as exertion, illness, repetitive activity or inadequate sleep.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.no_confusable_reason: No single interchangeable alternative is asserted for this complete source condition; related requirements keep separate nodes and their exact qualifiers.

nodes.label: Tiredness can impair vision and delay driving decisions; avoid driving when fatigued.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.no_confusable_reason: No single interchangeable alternative is asserted for this complete source condition; related requirements keep separate nodes and their exact qualifiers.

nodes.label: The handbook compares the performance loss from extended wakefulness with alcohol-related impairment and places responsibility on the driver to avoid tired driving.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.no_confusable_reason: No single interchangeable alternative is asserted for this complete source condition; related requirements keep separate nodes and their exact qualifiers.

nodes.label: For ordinary daytime alertness, the manual recommends adequate sleep and gives an average range of seven through nine hours.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: On a long journey, plan a break at least once every two hours to stretch or get a drink.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Before tiredness becomes severe, leave the road at an exit or rest area and take a fifteen-to-twenty-minute nap or find overnight accommodation.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Avoid late-night driving when possible and arrange for a companion to share the driving.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A distraction removes attention from driving; looking away, taking hands off the wheel and mentally disengaging can all increase crash risk.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The handheld-electronics prohibition covers a moving vehicle and brief traffic stops, including stops for traffic-control devices.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Prohibited handheld activities include electronic messaging, calls, internet requests, navigation-data entry and typing into portable electronic equipment.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Holding a voice-capable electronic device beside the ear while the vehicle moves creates a presumption that the driver is making a call.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Drivers under eighteen cannot use either handheld or hands-free mobile electronics while driving or briefly stopped in traffic, except to report an emergency to emergency dispatch or a public-safety agency.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A permitted hands-free conversation uses equipment that allows conversation without holding the device; the definition permits a hand to activate, deactivate or start a function.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The manual's permitted hands-free use still requires that the driver keep attention on the road ahead.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The listed electronics exceptions include action required by an ignition-interlock device.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Avoid arguments and emotionally stressful conversations with passengers while driving.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Do not eat behind the wheel; secure children with appropriate restraints and carry pets in a secured carrier or portable kennel.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The operator remains responsible for attentive and safe operation despite the presence of passengers or devices.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Aggressive driving involves intentionally taking an action that places another person's safety or property at risk.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Aggressive behaviors include speeding, close following, unsafe lane changes, improper signals and disregarding traffic controls.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Concentrate on operating the vehicle and show patience and courtesy toward other road users.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: For someone under twenty-one, the manual prohibits control of a vehicle while impaired by alcohol, controlled drugs, prescriptions, nonprescription drugs or other impairing substances.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The stated alcohol-concentration threshold for an operator under twenty-one is zero point zero two percent or greater.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A driver under twenty-one may transport alcoholic beverages only while accompanied by a parent, legal guardian or spouse of legal age, under the stated exception.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Alcohol and other impairing substances can diminish judgment, vision and reaction speed.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Impaired judgment makes clear, quick driving decisions harder to perform.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Alcohol-related visual effects can include blur, double vision, slow focusing and poorer estimates of distance, speed or movement.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: An impaired reaction slows the processing of information and the response to a driving task.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The handbook advises against driving any vehicle after consuming alcohol or impairing drugs and warns that even an initial drink can affect driving ability.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Prevent a friend or relative from driving after drinking or using an impairing drug.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Only time reduces alcohol's effects; coffee, meals, fresh air, exercise or cold showers may increase alertness without reversing impairment.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The handbook describes an initial impaired-driving conviction as a Class B misdemeanor with a fine of at least five hundred dollars and possible privilege loss lasting nine months through two years.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Restoration after the described initial impaired-driving offense requires attendance at an approved impaired-driver education course.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Repeat impaired-driving convictions carry stronger penalties, including larger fines and longer suspensions.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Nonprescription remedies for pain, colds, allergies or nervousness can cause drowsiness and affect driving.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Stimulant or diet pills can produce nervousness, dizziness, concentration problems or visual effects that interfere with driving.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Read a medicine's warnings before use, and ask a doctor or pharmacist about driving effects when uncertain.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Prescription medicines can impair reflexes, judgment, vision and alertness; the examples include antidepressants, pain medicines, sleep aids and sedatives.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Illegal drugs can impair driving functions, and driving under their influence is unlawful and dangerous.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Avoid alcohol while taking other drugs because their effects can combine with or amplify alcohol-related impairment.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Strong emotions, including worry, excitement, fear, anger or depression, can interfere with information processing and safe driving.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Calm down before driving; the handbook suggests a short walk or nap as possible ways to settle strong emotions.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Allow extra departure time and plan for traffic or poor weather to reduce stressful driving situations.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Let another person drive when emotions interfere with safe operation.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A parked vehicle starts heating immediately in warm weather and can become dangerously hot within minutes.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Do not leave a child alone in a vehicle for any duration.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Check the entire vehicle, with particular attention to the rear seat, before locking it and walking away.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Putting a personal item in the rear seat can serve as a reminder to inspect that seat before leaving the vehicle.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Keep keys and key fobs beyond children's reach and teach children that vehicles are not places to play.
